scope: External-background spatial aggregation transfer, not a source or gravity likelihood.
mean: One channel-wise constant estimated from all western pixels; no eastern or local mean subtraction.
covariance: For each side, tile each fixed 24x24 core into aligned disjoint squares, average residuals, and take western second moment. Fixed 10% diagonal shrinkage. No model selection or threshold tuning.
baseline: The western 1-pixel covariance divided by side squared: assumes spatially independent pixels but retains channel covariance.
metric: Equal-core mean of spectral quadratic form per 42 channels, marginal log density, and trace second moment. Report all 27 eastern cores and each of six scales.
controls: Explicit loop versus reshape aggregation; analytic independent and common-mode aperture covariance; inverse Gaussian quadratic/logdet reference; no validation data enter fitting; finite/rank-deficient covariance and invalid shapes.
limitations: Both sides previously exposed; this is development transfer, not new confirmation.
Within-core tiles, neighboring cores, and nested scales are not independent replications.
Large scales have only 29 training cores for 42 channels; fixed shrinkage is not a sample-size cure.
Second moments retain background mean/foreground errors; these are not certified pure instrument noise.
This defines marginal uncertainty for each aperture separately, not a coherent joint spatial cube covariance.
No stellar/gas mass, rotation or lensing score is generated.
